environment.description: Giant elliptical; uniquely approaching us at -244 km/s (blueshifted); falling into Virgo from far side; normal ICM environment

placement_notes.v0: Two systems in M86 outer stellar body. M86 is notably APPROACHING us (blueshifted by -244 km/s) — infalling from the far side of the Virgo cluster. Ram pressure from ICM wind acts on interstellar gas. Old metal-rich elliptical stars: rocky world bias, K hosts dominant. ICM ram-pressure wind may strip any residual interstellar material from young-star zones.
open_questions: M86 approaches us faster than expected — will it pass through the cluster core?
X-ray plume detected behind M86 from ram-pressure — does this affect very outer planetary orbits?
